sirsi gemma serve --status reported unavailable while the broker was demonstrably serving tokens
traced to gemmaServerStop deleting ~/.sirsi/gemma-server.port and gemmaAwaitWarm never restoring it
reproduced: rm ~/.sirsi/gemma-server.port; sirsi gemma serve -> port file stayed missing pre-fix

closure_evidence.product: N/A — infra reliability fix, no product surface change.
closure_evidence.technical: gemmaAwaitWarm (cmd/sirsi/gemma_serve.go) now writes ~/.sirsi/gemma-server.port on confirmed warm, mirroring the existing SyncGemmaPidFile pattern. Added TestGemmaAwaitWarmRestoresPortFile regression test.
closure_evidence.operational: No config/deploy change. Fix committed to fix/broker-quarantine (3d51b952), intentionally left unpushed — that branch is 141 commits ahead of origin with substantial unrelated uncommitted work already in the tree; pushing was left to the branch owner rather than done unprompted.
closure_evidence.narrative: The liveness-watch alert was a false positive caused by a latent bug: any stop/start cycle of the broker (including the watch's own prescribed auto-restore) deleted the port file that both --status and the liveness probes depend on, without ever recreating it. The broker itself was healthy throughout this incident.
